run.preReadNotes:
Open Mirror pre-read, FILTER MODE (default). Topic = the operating rules; comparison = the document's buoyancy/cavitation language.

Step 1 - Plain statement. Six integer counters (positions 1-6) with fixed capacities, an upper threshold and a lower threshold each, a two-valued flag per position (starts at value A = "LAMINAR"), and a running "lost" tally starting at 0. Five rounds, each of five ordered phases: (1) add a per-round per-position input from a table, no cap; (2) sequential spill pass 1->6: anything above capacity is moved to the next higher position, from position 6 it goes to the lost tally; (3) flag update with hysteresis: A->B when value >= upper threshold, B->A when value <= lower threshold, otherwise unchanged; (4) simultaneous drain: compute floor(value/4) for A positions, floor(value/2) for B positions, all from the same snapshot; subtract; A drains go to the lost tally, B drains go to the next lower position (position 1's B drain goes to lost); no cap; (5) if the grand total exceeds 38, halve every position (floor) and add the removed units to lost. Conservation: start + inputs = end + lost. The document's own embedded comparison (it describes the line "entirely in buoyancy and cavitation terms") is pulled out as the picture set; the literal rules stay. No instructions aimed at me were found inside the operating document. The plain restatement fully specifies the job, so by the rule a filter run could stop here; pictures are run below anyway for the desk record.

Step 2 - Pictures (taken from the document's own vocabulary): P1 cavitation (inception/desinence marks, LAMINAR/CAVITATING), P2 ballast compartments with scuppers (volume, overflow aft), P3 emergency blow (blowing ballast).

Step 3/4 - Map and break.
P1 Cavitation: matches - inception/desinence = two thresholds with hysteresis (real cavitation does show inception vs desinence hysteresis). Question it eases: does a position stay in its state between the marks? Break: real cavitation is driven by pressure/flow speed, not by fill level, and does not double pumping throughput or reverse flow "forward" into the next tank; real cavitation reduces pump output. A reader importing real practice would expect cavitating pumps to pump LESS, contradicting the stated rule (half, backflowed). Marked misleading at this break point if used to infer behaviour.
P2 Ballast compartments/scuppers: matches - capacity, overflow passing to a neighbour, last one overboard. Break: real scuppers drain overboard or to bilge, not into the adjacent tank; real tanks cannot exceed volume (the document explicitly allows over-volume after fill and after backflow). Importing physical capacity limits would contradict the stated "volume not enforced" rules. Misleading if used to enforce volume outside Step 2.
P3 Emergency blow: matches - a trigger on total ballast that dumps water. Break: a real blow empties tanks fully, not halving with floor; trigger is depth/emergency, not a sum > 38. Strips back to the rule as stated.

Step 5 - What survives: P1 - the flag has memory between two thresholds. P2 - excess moves one position higher in a single ordered pass, and can chain. P3 - a global total check halves everything.

Step 6 - Grade: P1 adds nothing (the hysteresis is stated plainly in Step 3); also misleading if real cavitation is substituted. P2 adds nothing (the chaining is stated in Step 2); misleading if real capacity limits are imported. P3 adds nothing.
Adds nothing: 3 of 3. Misleading: 0 as used here (P1 and P2 would become misleading only if real-world practice were substituted, which the desk lead forbids; noted in one line each). Not run: 0.

Step 7 - Keep exploring: (empty). Hold: (empty). Discard: (empty). Notes for the desk: do not let the cavitation picture suggest reduced pumping or the tank picture suggest volume caps outside Step 2. The pre-read does not check facts and recommends nothing.
run.rulesInOwnWords:
Setup: six compartments, contents start [3,6,6,2,2,1]; volumes [10,8,12,6,9,7]; inception [7,6,9,5,7,5]; desinence [3,2,4,2,3,2]; all pumps LAMINAR; Total Overboard (TO) = 0. Each of 5 cycles:
1. Fill: add that cycle's fill row to each compartment. No cap.
2. Scupper: go 1 to 6 in order. If contents > volume, set to volume and add the excess to compartment n+1 (from 6, add to TO). Since it is sequential, overflow can cascade aft in the same pass.
3. State check on post-scupper contents: LAMINAR with contents >= inception -> CAVITATING; CAVITATING with contents <= desinence -> LAMINAR; otherwise unchanged (hysteresis band keeps the old state). Log each change.
4. Pumping: from a single snapshot, pumped = floor(c/4) if LAMINAR, floor(c/2) if CAVITATING. Then simultaneously: subtract each pumped amount; LAMINAR amounts go to TO; CAVITATING amounts go to compartment n-1 (compartment 1's goes to TO). No cap.
5. Blow check: if total contents > 38, halve each compartment (floor) and add all removed units to TO; log the cycle. Exactly 38 does not fire.
Report end contents, states, change log, blow cycles, TO, and balance: start sum + fill sum = end sum + TO.

run.notes: I used a short Python script for the arithmetic and then checked every cycle by hand. Edge cases: in cycle 5 the end total was exactly 38, so the blow did not fire. Cycle 4 had a scupper cascade through all six compartments. In cycle 2, compartments 3 and 5 sat exactly on their desinence marks (4 and 3) and reverted to LAMINAR, and compartment 1 sat exactly on its inception mark (7) and went to CAVITATING. I applied the document's rules as written, including that cavitating pumps drain half and send it forward, and I did not substitute real-world cavitation behaviour.
